question: Can category-theoretic compositional models provide one language for comparing deterministic, probabilistic, causal, linguistic, neural, and quantum AI systems, and can interpreted string-diagram components yield reliable explanations of their behavior?

key_findings.claim: The paper supplies an unusually broad and internally coherent notation for separating a model's abstract syntax from its concrete implementation across many AI families.
key_findings.evidence: A compositional model consists of a signature of variables, generators, and equations, the freely generated structure category, a semantics category, and a structure-preserving representation functor. The paper instantiates this template for classifiers, encoder-decoders, linear and rule-based models, neural networks, transformers, sequence models, DisCoCat, DisCoCirc, conceptual spaces, causal models, functional causal models, and quantum processes. This is a valuable synthesis and translation layer; it is not an empirical finding that these representations improve accuracy, transparency, or safety.

key_findings.claim: Casting a model as a string diagram does not make it interpretable; almost any computational graph admits many decompositions, so the substantive work lies in selecting a useful level and justifying its human meanings.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly observe that a neural network can always be rendered as a huge diagram and that abstraction can range from a single black box to individual neurons. Their CI designation then depends on whether every chosen variable and generator receives a human-friendly interpretation. Since refinements and abstraction levels are non-unique, the formalism alone neither selects the right modules nor prevents a verbose, arbitrary, misleading, or vacuous decomposition.

key_findings.claim: The central definition of interpretation is explicitly not fully formal and provides no test that a purported human-friendly meaning is correct, useful, faithful, or understandable to an intended audience.
key_findings.evidence: An interpretation is a human-friendly signature plus partial abstract and concrete maps. Page 25 states that the definition is 'not fully formal' because human-friendly is unspecified; later discussion assigns the researcher, user, or explainee responsibility for deciding meaningfulness. Commutativity only makes abstract and concrete labels agree where both are defined. It does not require empirical fidelity, causal validity, robustness, brevity, audience comprehension, task relevance, or agreement among annotators. Complete interpretation therefore means complete coverage by labels, not validated interpretability.

key_findings.claim: Interpretations are not required to preserve equations or composition, so the paper's formal definition does not ensure that interpretations themselves compose.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines a partial map of signatures while explicitly dropping the requirement to map equations, and its default interpretation maps are such partial maps. It discusses a functorial interpretation that could preserve monoidal structure, but declines to make it the default because human terms may not form a category. Consequently, two individually named components may compose in a way with no corresponding human-level meaning, and a diagram equality in the model need not be an equation in the human signature. The adjective compositional describes the model syntax more rigorously than it describes the interpretation.

anchors.section: Partial maps of signatures and Definition 5

key_findings.claim: No-influence arguments provide a real deductive guarantee, but only for a faithful channel diagram whose relevant dependencies, shared state, and latent inputs have all been represented.
key_findings.evidence: For diagrams of channels, absence of a directed path from input X to output Y allows discards to be pushed through the diagram and proves structural no-influence. This is mathematically useful for sparse causal and DisCoCirc structures. It is not a general explanation of dense neural behavior, and omitted global state, parameter sharing, normalization, memory, common causes, or an incorrect decomposition can invalidate the intended dependency reading. The guarantee concerns the represented model, not the modeled world, a distinction the paper itself emphasizes.

key_findings.claim: Diagram surgery is a helpful umbrella for probes, ablations, and component replacement, but an arbitrary diagram edit is not automatically a causal intervention or an explanation.
key_findings.evidence: The definition permits replacing any fragment and even changing its input/output types, yielding a new related model. The section recasts probes, internal classifiers, do-interventions, input counterfactuals, and word/component substitutions as surgery. This unifies notation, but explanatory force is supplied externally by an interpretation and a valid comparison; arbitrary edits may be off-distribution, non-identifiable, confounded, or incomparable. Calling all such modifications interventions risks transferring causal connotations beyond the causal-model assumptions that justify them.

key_findings.claim: Rewrite explanations are deductively sound when their interpreted equations are true, but the practical contribution is conditional and presently unvalidated.
key_findings.evidence: A rewrite explanation is defined as interpreted diagram equations plus a rewriting proof that they imply an exact or approximate output equality. For rules and causal toy models, this largely recovers tracing through an intrinsically interpretable model. For learned sequence and DisCoCirc models, the key equations are assumed, hard-coded, encouraged by a loss, or proposed to be discovered after training. The authors call this their most speculative technique and repeatedly state that useful learned CI models and rewrite explanations remain to be demonstrated. No algorithm finds equations, tests human meaning, controls multiple-hypothesis search, or measures explanation quality.

key_findings.claim: The paper's approximate rewrite relation is only an informal placeholder and does not supply usable end-to-end error guarantees.
key_findings.evidence: Remark 40 says approximation should be quantified and respected by composition, then treats it informally, pointing to a normed quantum-process construction as one possible formalization. In a deep learned composition, local approximation errors can amplify with operator norms, depth, branching, distribution shift, and shared components. The paper gives no metric for heterogeneous classical/probabilistic/quantum morphisms, no accumulation theorem, no uncertainty, and no threshold for when an approximate proof remains explanatory.

key_findings.claim: The model-versus-world distinction is one of the paper's strongest reusable contributions and appropriately limits what its own diagrammatic guarantees mean.
key_findings.evidence: The authors distinguish M-type explanations about a model from W-type explanations about the phenomenon. A feature attribution, no-influence proof, or surgery result can be exact for a predictor yet fail to guide real-world action if the diagram omits the world's causal structure. The stroke and loan examples make this misuse concrete. The paper further argues that ordinary counterfactual explanations are alternative model inputs, not Pearlian counterfactuals, unless an additional causal data-generating model licenses the intervention and same-world comparison.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript is theory, synthesis, and a research agenda rather than a validated XAI method.
key_findings.evidence: Across 106 pages it gives definitions and illustrative diagrams but no trained model produced by the framework, benchmark, human study, explanation-fidelity test, statistical analysis, runtime comparison, or end-user task. The conclusion explicitly leaves finding CI models, learning compositional structure, practical rewrite explanations, model relations, and compositional generalization to future work. The breadth of examples demonstrates expressivity of the notation, not that the proposed explanations are discoverable, scalable, legible, or useful.

key_findings.claim: The categorical treatment includes quantum models uniformly, but this is mathematical generality rather than evidence of explainable or useful quantum AI.
key_findings.evidence: The semantics category can be chosen as quantum processes, and the paper shows neural and quantum implementations of the same text circuit. It also acknowledges that generic density operators lack concrete human interpretations, that useful quantum-model applications remain uncertain, and that probing may disturb a state. No quantum model is trained or evaluated here. The framework prevents classical copying assumptions from being silently reused, but it does not solve quantum semantic interpretation.

key_findings.claim: The appendix's formal definition of refinement contains an ill-typed equality, so that part of the promised model-relation theory is not valid as printed.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 55 gives a functor R from the structure category induced by D to that induced by D', then requires R(D)=R(D'). But D' belongs to the codomain structure category, so R(D') is undefined; the intended condition is presumably R(D)=D' (together with semantic commutation). The same appendix calls its causal-abstraction discussion incomplete and defers a full categorical account. This does not invalidate the main compositional-model definition, but it materially limits the refinement formalism used to relate abstraction levels.

key_findings.claim: A direct 2023 categorical-XAI prior substantially narrows the unification novelty, while a separate causal-abstraction prior offers a more falsifiable route to internal meaning.
key_findings.evidence: Barbiero et al. (arXiv:2304.14094), which the paper cites but describes mainly through learning lenses, already advertises categorical syntax-to-semantics formalization, a definition of explanation, modeling of XAI architectures, and intrinsic/post-hoc taxonomy. Geiger et al. (arXiv:2301.04709), apparently uncited by ID/title, defines high-level algorithms as faithful causal abstractions and tests them interventionally. The defensible novelty here is the exact complete-interpretation/CI packaging, its deterministic-probabilistic-quantum survey, and the trio of no-influence, general diagram surgery, and rewrite explanations—not categorical unification of XAI in general.

anchors.section: Categories for AI and categorical XAI

key_findings.claim: Later work confirms both the value and the missing constraints of the proposal: unrestricted alignment maps can be vacuous, while measurable faithfulness and complexity make compositional interpretation testable.
key_findings.evidence: Sutter et al. (2025) show that expressive nonlinear maps can make arbitrary or random representations satisfy causal abstractions, demonstrating why an unpenalized chosen Human mapping is insufficient evidence. Gauderis et al. (2026) explicitly builds on this paper and adds commuting syntactic/semantic mappings, quantitative compositional faithfulness and complexity, MDL, constrained optimization, and compressive refinement. These papers do not erase this paper's conceptual priority, but they identify the operational controls required to turn it into a falsifiable method.

method.core_idea: Represent a trained AI model as a structure-preserving map from a freely generated diagrammatic syntax into a chosen semantic category, attach partial human interpretations to variables and processes, and use visible factorization plus equations to reason about influence, interventions, and outputs.
method.mechanism: A signature lists typed variables, generator boxes, and diagram equations. Its free monoidal, copy-discard, Markov, rigid, closed, or higher-order category gives the abstract model structure; a functor assigns deterministic functions, stochastic channels, neural networks, linear maps, or quantum processes as semantics. A Human signature and partial abstract/concrete maps label components. Complete coverage defines a compositionally-interpretable model. Compositional frameworks specify permitted queries such as marginalization, conditioning, intervention, and counterfactuals. Explanation then uses path-based no-influence proofs, replacement/probing of diagram fragments, or rewrite proofs from interpreted exact/approximate equations.
assumptions: A useful model decomposition and abstraction level are known or can be selected by a researcher.
Human-friendly terms can be identified despite no formal or empirical criterion in the definition.
Component labels faithfully describe their semantic behavior, not merely a preferred story about them.
All dependencies relevant to an influence claim are explicit in the diagram and every represented box is a valid channel where required.
A model-level diagram is not mistaken for structure in the world unless an additional correspondence is justified.
Exact equations really hold in the semantics, or approximate equations have a metric stable under composition.
Interpretable local equations can be found, imposed, or learned without destroying task utility.
A composition of interpreted components remains intelligible even though interpretation maps are not required to be functorial.
Diagram surgery preserves enough context for comparisons to be meaningful and does not introduce pathological off-distribution states.
A complete interpretation is preferable to a sparse but better validated explanation.
The categorical formalism's cross-domain generality is useful enough to offset its abstraction and notation costs.
Quantum and classical semantics can be compared at the structural level despite different observability and copying constraints.

techniques.role: Declares typed variables, primitive processes, and equations as a model's abstract vocabulary.
Generates all legal string diagrams and equates them under the declared rewrite rules.
Maps syntax into deterministic, stochastic, neural, linear, or quantum semantics while preserving composition.
Assigns human terms to selected abstract variables and generators.
Assigns human terms to selected semantic morphisms and, for concretely interpreted variables, all states.
Calls a model compositionally interpretable when every variable and generator has an abstract interpretation.
Separates a model's diagram from the queries and operations permitted by input-output, probabilistic, or causal frameworks.
Proves no-influence by connectivity and discard equations in channel diagrams.
Copies or measures an internal wire and maps it to an interpreted probe variable.
Replaces model fragments to express ablations, interventions, alternate inputs, and component edits.
Explains an output through a sequence of exact interpreted diagram equations.
Extends rewriting informally to quantified approximate equations stable under composition.
Distinguishes statements about predictor behavior from claims about the modeled phenomenon.
Shows why an alternate model input is not a Pearlian counterfactual without a causal generator for inputs.
Attempts to relate coarse and fine diagrams via semantics-preserving model morphisms.
Uses intervention-commuting high/low alignments as a stronger route to interpreted neural representations.

evaluations.setting: Deterministic, probabilistic, neural, linguistic, causal, conceptual-space, and quantum model families.
evaluations.metric: Constructive coverage by a common signature/structure/semantics definition.
evaluations.result: The paper successfully writes a wide range of familiar models as compositional models, demonstrating expressivity of the notation but not a comparative performance or interpretability gain.
evaluations.baseline: The original family-specific mathematical descriptions and computational graphs.

evaluations.setting: Rule lists, decision trees, linear models, and causal diagrams.
evaluations.metric: Whether existing intrinsic transparency can be recovered as interpreted string-diagram components.
evaluations.result: Their familiar step-by-step or coefficient/mechanism explanations fit naturally, supporting the framework's descriptive face validity.
evaluations.baseline: Conventional intrinsic-interpretability accounts without category-theoretic notation.

evaluations.setting: Sparse channel and causal diagrams with disconnected input-output paths.
evaluations.metric: Exact derivability of no-influence by discard rewriting.
evaluations.result: Absence of a directed path proves structural no-influence in the represented channel model.
evaluations.baseline: Manual dependency inspection and standard causal DAG ancestry/do-calculus reasoning.

evaluations.setting: RNN probing, causal mechanism replacement, alternate model inputs, and DisCoCirc word edits.
evaluations.metric: Ability to express diverse internal and external interventions as diagram surgery.
evaluations.result: The notation unifies these modifications, but no fidelity, efficiency, statistical validity, or human usefulness experiment is performed.
evaluations.baseline: Probes, ablations, activation interventions, CFEs, and causal do-interventions in their native formalisms.

evaluations.setting: Rule-based, causal, sequence, conceptual-space, and DisCoCirc toy models.
evaluations.metric: Existence of an interpreted equation sequence proving the output.
evaluations.result: Exact toy rewrite proofs are shown; learned-model examples assume the crucial semantic equations and have no trained artifact or validation.
evaluations.baseline: Tracing through an intrinsically interpretable model or supplying an informal natural-language rationale.

evaluations.setting: Counterfactual explanations for tabular prediction and Pearlian structural causal models.
evaluations.metric: Formal equivalence of input substitution with abduction-action-prediction counterfactual semantics.
evaluations.result: The appendix shows that changing one predictor input is not generally a Pearlian counterfactual because an omitted causal input model may change descendants and exogenous-state conditioning.
evaluations.baseline: Common CFE rhetoric treating a close alternate input as 'had this feature been different'.

evaluations.setting: Classical neural and quantum circuit realizations of the same compositional text structure.
evaluations.metric: Uniform representability by changing the semantics category.
evaluations.result: Both implementations share abstract syntax, while concrete interpretation and non-disturbing probing become harder for quantum states; no task experiment is run.
evaluations.baseline: Separate classical computational-graph and quantum-circuit descriptions.

evaluations.setting: Official arXiv source artifact rebuilt from the submitted TeX and pre-generated bibliography.
evaluations.metric: Static source completeness and PDF compilation.
evaluations.result: The source compiles to 106 pages and all referenced diagram assets resolve, but the bibliography database is missing, 118 editorial TODO comments remain, and there is no paper-specific implementation or empirical artifact.
evaluations.baseline: A provenance-complete theoretical artifact with bibliography source, tagged revision, and executable examples/tests.

limitations: Author-stated: the definition is not fully formal because it does not define what makes a term human-friendly.
Author-stated: useful learned CI models and nontrivial rewrite explanations remain to be demonstrated in practice.
Author-stated: finding or learning meaningful compositional structure is an open problem.
Author-stated: approximate diagram equality is treated informally and needs a quantified composition-compatible notion.
Author-stated: generic quantum representation states do not have obvious concrete interpretations and probing may disturb them.
Reviewer inference: no empirical model, benchmark, user study, fidelity test, statistical analysis, or runtime/complexity comparison validates the framework.
Reviewer inference: any model admits many string-diagram refinements, so the formalism does not select an explanatory abstraction level.
Reviewer inference: complete label coverage does not establish correctness, faithfulness, stability, usefulness, or audience understanding.
Reviewer inference: interpretation maps need not preserve equations or composition, weakening the central compositional-interpretation claim.
Reviewer inference: strict no-influence depends on an explicit, faithful channel decomposition and cannot reveal parameter-specific cancellations or omitted shared state.
Reviewer inference: arbitrary diagram surgery is broader than causal intervention and may generate off-distribution or semantically incomparable models.
Reviewer inference: rewrite proofs can be circular if equations are selected because they restate the desired output or discovered on the same examples being explained.
Reviewer inference: approximate local equations lack an error-composition theorem for deep heterogeneous diagrams.
Reviewer inference: dense 106-page diagrams demonstrate formal expressivity but not cognitive scalability or reduced explanation complexity.
Reviewer inference: the exact CI label is novel, but a 2023 categorical-XAI paper already claimed syntax/semantics unification and formal explanation.
Formal audit: Definition 55's refinement condition applies R to a codomain diagram D', making the printed equality ill-typed.
Artifact audit: the source omits CI.bib and relies on a generated main.bbl; it has no version-control revision, code, tests, or executable examples.
Source audit: 118 editorial TODO/FIXME comments and zero theorem/proposition/lemma environments emphasize the manuscript's agenda/synthesis status rather than invalidating its definitions.
failure_modes: A researcher can attach plausible names to arbitrary internal components and thereby obtain a complete but false interpretation.
A highly expressive alignment map can make a random or unrelated representation appear perfectly faithful.
Refining a model into many small boxes can increase diagram complexity without improving human understanding.
Choosing a single black-box generator makes the same model compositionally trivial and hides useful mechanisms.
Two interpreted components can compose into behavior with no stable human-level meaning because interpretation is not functorial.
An omitted shared parameter, normalization statistic, cache, random seed, or latent cause can invalidate a path-based no-influence claim.
A model-level causal-looking diagram can be mistaken for the causal structure of the world and yield harmful action advice.
A surgery intervention can create an internal state the model never encounters naturally and support a misleading explanation.
A probe can learn information present in a representation without showing that the base model uses that information.
A rewrite rule can be selected post hoc to fit the explained instance and fail on counterexamples or distribution shift.
Approximation error can grow through repeated composition until the final claimed output relation is meaningless.
A long formally correct rewrite can be less comprehensible than a short approximate explanation.
A quantum measurement used for interpretation can disturb the very state whose causal role is being assessed.
A CFE can recommend an infeasible feature change because it ignores the causal generator and dependencies among inputs.
An ill-typed or underspecified model-refinement map can make comparisons across abstraction levels formally ambiguous.
A categorical encoding can appear rigorous while merely renaming existing XAI operations without adding validation or predictive constraints.
reusable_insights: Separate syntax, semantics, and human interpretation explicitly; most interpretability disputes conflate at least two of them.
Require every explanation to declare whether it is about model behavior or the modeled world.
Treat decomposition selection as an optimization over faithfulness, complexity, stability, and audience usefulness rather than a free modeling choice.
Make interpretation maps compositional where possible, and measure their equation-preservation error where exact functoriality is impossible.
Validate component meanings with interventions and held-out counterexamples, not labels or probes alone.
Use path-based no-influence as a certified negative claim only after explicitly accounting for shared/global state and hidden inputs.
Distinguish probes, ablations, substitutions, causal interventions, and world interventions even if one diagrammatic syntax can express all of them.
For learned rewrite explanations, preregister the equation-discovery data and test proofs on disjoint inputs to prevent post-hoc tautologies.
Track local approximation bounds through composition using operator sensitivity or probabilistic confidence, and reject explanations whose end-to-end bound is too loose.
Compare against always-valid baselines: native computational graphs, rule traces, causal abstraction, concept bottlenecks, mechanistic circuits, and human-authored explanations.
Use equation-based model design to make desired invariants testable and modular, but keep task accuracy and falsification suites independent.
Represent scientific or RL environments compositionally so simulator modules, reward checks, validators, and interventions can be swapped and audited separately.
For evolving synthetic environments, log which structural equations are hard constraints, learned approximations, or empirical observations.
Prefer minimal explanatory subdiagrams over complete coverage and report the unexplained residual explicitly.
Use causal-abstraction mappings with complexity penalties and negative controls such as random networks to prevent vacuous alignments.
Package theoretical diagram assets with executable semantic checks so every claimed equality can be mechanically tested.
open_questions: How should human-friendly meaning be operationalized for a specific user, task, and decision without collapsing into subjective annotation?
Can one learn a minimal string-diagram decomposition from behavior while avoiding arbitrary refinements and nonlinear alignment vacuity?
What compositional faithfulness and complexity objective best balances exactness with cognitive usefulness?
Which interpretation equations should be hard-coded, softly trained, or discovered after training, and how can discovery avoid leakage?
How should approximation errors and statistical uncertainty compose across deep, recurrent, stochastic, or branching diagrams?
Can rewrite explanations be automatically minimized and translated into natural language without losing their proof guarantee?
Do human users make better calibrated decisions with diagrammatic explanations than with native rule traces, causal graphs, or mechanistic circuits?
How robust are inferred component meanings across seeds, retraining, model scaling, prompt changes, and distribution shifts?
Can diagram surgery be given intervention semantics that separate in-distribution causal tests from arbitrary component edits?
How can global variables, parameter sharing, memory, normalization, and asynchronous state be represented without destroying diagram readability?
What negative controls reliably detect arbitrary Human mappings, including random models, label permutations, and overly expressive alignments?
Can CI-style equations validate learning signal in a synthetic RL environment before expensive policy training?
Which local environment invariants predict downstream learning progress and scaling across policy/model sizes?
Can evolutionary environment search optimize diversity and learning progress while maintaining mechanically checked compositional constraints?
When is human review indispensable for assigning semantics, and when can theorem checking, interventions, or external measurements replace it?
How should classical explanations of quantum models account for measurement disturbance and inaccessible internal state?

competitive_landscape.title: Backprop as Functor: A compositional perspective on supervised learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational categorical account of composing learning systems and backpropagation, cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: It formalizes training rather than human interpretation or XAI; the target fixes trained semantics and studies explanatory structure.

competitive_landscape.title: Categorical Foundations of Gradient-Based Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: General parameterized-lens formalism for categorical learning, acknowledged as enabling substrate.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies compositional optimization machinery; the target deliberately analyzes model structure after training and adds interpretation maps.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Abstraction Error and a Category of Causal Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 categorical causal abstraction with a quantitative compositional error and error bounds.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is narrower than general CI but offers the validation metric and approximate-composition discipline missing from the target's subjective Human maps.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Aligns neural representations with interpretable high-level causal variables and tests them through interchange interventions.
competitive_landscape.difference: This cited prior is narrower but substantially more operational and falsifiable than declaring an abstract interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Inducing Causal Structure for Interpretable Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Trains networks with interchange interventions and provides a zero-loss causal-abstraction guarantee.
competitive_landscape.difference: It already gives an operational answer to learning meaningful structure for a specified high-level model; the target generalizes the agenda beyond causal models but leaves training open.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Explanations and XAI
competitive_landscape.relationship: Formal account of sufficient, counterfactual, and action-guiding explanations cited in the target's XAI discussion.
competitive_landscape.difference: It grounds explanation in causal purpose and action; the target covers more model families and diagram operations but has a broader, less operational explanation criterion.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Defines intelligible high-level algorithms as interventionally faithful simplifications of low-level mechanisms, including distributed/polysemantic mappings.
competitive_landscape.difference: This likely uncited prior is causally narrower but supplies a testable faithfulness condition that the target's chosen Human signature lacks.

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Distributed Alignment Search learns and validates mappings from internal states to human-specified causal variables.
competitive_landscape.difference: It searches and tests interpretations rather than assuming labels; the target offers a broader categorical vocabulary and noncausal model families.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal models in string diagrams
competitive_landscape.relationship: Same-author technical substrate for interventions, counterfactuals, channels, and causal diagram surgery.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target's novelty is the XAI synthesis and CI/rewrite packaging, not the underlying categorical causal calculus.

competitive_landscape.title: Categorical Foundations of Explainable AI: A Unifying Theory
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strongest direct prior: categorical free syntax and semantic instantiation, formal explanation, XAI architectures, and intrinsic/post-hoc taxonomy.
competitive_landscape.difference: The target cites but under-compares it; target's residue is the exact complete-interpretation/CI notion, wider deterministic-probabilistic-quantum survey, and influence/surgery/rewrite trio.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability is in the Mind of the Beholder: A Causal Framework for Human-interpretable Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Observer-relative vocabulary and alignment framework with an operational name-transfer game.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is closest to the target's Human signature but explicitly tests observer-relative meaning; the target embeds more compositional structure while leaving human-friendly undefined.

competitive_landscape.title: Position: Categorical Deep Learning is an Algebraic Theory of All Architectures
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-v1 categorical architecture-unification thesis cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: It weakens novelty of cross-architecture categorical coverage; the target distinctly adds human interpretation and XAI arguments.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Compositionality in Concept Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: One-day-later independent empirical work on compositional concept learning.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is not a fair prior and is much narrower, but tests whether learned concepts compose rather than defining complete interpretation by coverage.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Anatomy of Attention
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent systematic categorical diagramming of attention variants with architectural recombination experiments.
competitive_landscape.difference: It operationalizes one architecture family; the target gives a much broader survey and interpretation framework without experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: A Pattern Language for Machine Learning Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent executable task equations and loss constraints, explicitly cited as upcoming in the target source.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies a concrete route for training equation-respecting components and latent editing; the target frames the interpretation and rewrite-explanation agenda.

competitive_landscape.title: Validating Mechanistic Interpretations: An Axiomatic Approach
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent axiomatization of approximate compositional semantics validated on an established case and a 2-SAT transformer.
competitive_landscape.difference: It provides faithfulness tests and empirical validation absent from the target's interpretation maps and informal approximate rewrites.

competitive_landscape.title: Combining Causal Models for More Accurate Abstractions of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Combines simple causal hypotheses and explicitly trades simplicity against faithfulness on GPT-2-small.
competitive_landscape.difference: It handles partial and input-dependent mechanisms more flexibly than binary complete interpretation; the target remains model-family general.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards a Comparative Framework for Compositional AI Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct empirical follow-on comparing compositional generalization and interpretation for quantum and neural DisCoCirc models.
competitive_landscape.difference: It turns part of the target's proposal into bAbI-derived comparative tests, while remaining narrower than the general theory.

competitive_landscape.title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct negative result showing expressive maps can make arbitrary or random models look perfectly aligned.
competitive_landscape.difference: It demonstrates the need for complexity constraints and negative controls absent from the target's unscored, user-chosen Human mappings.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal and Compositional Abstraction
competitive_landscape.relationship: Same-author formal follow-up using natural transformations for query- and component-level abstraction across causal and quantum models.
competitive_landscape.difference: It fills the target's explicitly deferred model-relation/abstraction theory and confirms that Appendix C was programmatic.

competitive_landscape.title: From Mechanistic to Compositional Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest direct successor, explicitly building on the target with compositional faithfulness, complexity, MDL, and compressive refinement.
competitive_landscape.difference: It preserves the target's conceptual priority but operationalizes and largely supersedes its nonformal interpretation core.

competitive_landscape.title: Certified Interventional Fidelity: Anytime-Valid, Adaptive Evaluation of Causal Claims in Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Statistical validation framework for intervention, activation-patching, and causal-abstraction claims.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies anytime-valid confidence and adaptive testing for the evidence layer missing from the target's diagram-surgery examples.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a comprehensive category-theoretic view of AI models and interpretation, introduces compositionally-interpretable models, and proposes influence constraints, general diagram surgery, and especially rewrite explanations as benefits unavailable to black boxes.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact package of a complete abstract interpretation over a compositional model, the model-versus-world analysis across deterministic/probabilistic/quantum semantics, and the named rewrite-explanation definition appear distinctive. However, categorical syntax/semantics unification and formal XAI explanation were already claimed by arXiv:2304.14094; causal-abstraction work already learned and interventionally validated mappings to human variables; same-author causal string diagrams supplied much of the surgery calculus. The target cites most of this substrate but does not adequately compare its unifying claim to the 2023 categorical-XAI paper and appears not to cite arXiv:2301.04709.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is moderate as a synthesis and conceptual taxonomy, with a narrower genuinely new residue in the exact CI/complete-interpretation terminology and rewrite-explanation packaging. Practical-method novelty is low because no learning, equation discovery, validation, metric, or user-facing implementation is supplied. Later work adding faithfulness, complexity, and statistical tests is best read as operationalizing—not erasing—the paper's conceptual agenda.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text and artifact pass completed 2026-08-23. All 106/106 extracted pages were read. Every page was rendered and visually inspected in nine contact sheets, with individual source/text inspection for definitions, examples, caveats, and appendices; this covered all nine numbered figures, all numbered equations through Equation 72, and the dense unnumbered string-diagram examples. The official arXiv source tarball SHA-256 is 92d8be09403366167dcf34e4442fae8bef34bd6a577dd8a36872df5b0d03f31a. It unpacked to 719 files including the tarball: 687 TikZ assets, 16 TeX files, 10 PNGs, one JPEG, one style file, TikZiT definitions/styles, and main.bbl. A clean LaTeX build using the supplied main.bbl succeeded and produced 106 pages (rebuilt PDF SHA-256 2eee9397350cc4b09785a05c318cb9ef6849a8ae53871020be361a83b2b33f8d); the build resolved 244 unique referenced TikZ files and seven referenced raster images. CI.bib is absent, so the bibliography cannot be regenerated, and source inspection found 118 editorial TODO/FIXME comments plus no theorem/proposition/lemma environments.
